@keep_lazy_text
def wrap(text, width):
    """
    A word-wrap function that preserves existing line breaks. Expects that
    existing line breaks are posix newlines.

    Preserve all white space except added line breaks consume the space on
    which they break the line.

    Don't wrap long words, thus the output text may have lines longer than
    ``width``.
    """

    import textwrap

    def my_wrap(text, width):
        wrapper = textwrap.TextWrapper(width=width, break_long_words=False, break_on_hyphens=False, replace_whitespace=False)
        lines = text.splitlines()
        wrapped_lines = []
        for line in lines:
            wrapped_lines.extend(wrapper.wrap(line))
        return wrapped_lines

    return '\n'.join(my_wrap(text, width))
